The post My 3D Printing Adventure Begins appeared first on SC Makes.
item.content:encoded:
After years of admiring from a distance, I’ve finally taken the plunge into the world of 3D printing, and what a world it is! My journey begins with the highly-acclaimed Bambu Labs X1 Carbon, a machine that promises speed, multi-color printing, and a level of precision that feels almost like magic. The future of making is here, and I’m thrilled to be a part of it. All of these initial prints were made using the Bambu Labs PLA that came with the printer, and the results have been incredible. The potential feels endless, and the only limit is my own imagination.

To get started, I tackled the three prints every new maker needs to experience.

The Benchy: A Rite of Passage

My very first print was, of course, a Benchy. For those unfamiliar, a Benchy is a small model boat designed specifically to test the capabilities and calibration of a 3D printer. It has tiny details, overhangs, and complex curves that push the machine to its limits. Seeing the X1C handle this test with ease was an incredible moment. It’s the official welcoming ceremony into the community, and my Benchy came out looking fantastic.

Practicality First: A Raspberry Pi Case

My second project was a bit more practical, taking me from a beginner to a designer. I’ve been working on a Raspberry Pi 4 project and needed a case that was both protective and functional. Instead of simply downloading a pre-made file, I decided to take on the challenge of designing my own. I used Fusion 360, a powerful CAD software, to model the case from scratch, meticulously measuring the Raspberry Pi to ensure a perfect fit. I made sure to include custom cutouts for easy access to the GPIO pins and to allow for proper airflow to the heatsinks. I even raised the board inside the bottom part for proper airflow around and below the board. Finally, I added an embedded label directly into the top cover for a clean, professional finish.

Once the design was complete, the next step was to get the model ready for the printer. I exported the file from Fusion 360 as a 3MF, which is often a better format for preserving model details than a traditional STL. From there, I imported it into Bambu Studio, the slicing software for my printer. This is where I truly felt the power of the X1 Carbon’s ecosystem. I discovered the time-lapse feature, which uses the built-in camera to automatically capture the entire printing process. The ability to design and produce a perfectly tailored solution for my electronics project—and record the entire process—is exactly why I got into this hobby.

A Blast from the Past: The Ocarina

For my third print, I wanted to do something special that combined my love for technology with my passion for video games. I chose to print a functional ocarina from one of my all-time favorite games, The Legend of Zelda. Finding the right model was key, as it needed to be designed with a precisely calibrated, hollow chamber for the sound to work correctly. The intricate shape and hollow chamber required an incredible level of accuracy from the printer. The Bambu Labs X1 Carbon delivered perfectly, its precision critical to maintaining the correct internal dimensions for proper tuning. A true test of the machine’s capabilities was its ability to print the hollow interior without any supports, which would have been impossible to remove. This was a testament to the printer’s excellent bridging and overhang performance.

Another significant challenge was the print’s form factor—it’s tall and narrow. This makes it prone to detaching from the build plate mid-print. Thankfully, the printer’s textured PEI plate provided excellent adhesion. The slightly rough surface gripped the plastic firmly, ensuring the ocarina remained perfectly stable and upright from the first layer to the last. Watching the nozzle delicately build the thin walls of the instrument layer by layer, knowing that any small error could ruin the acoustics or cause a print failure, was truly mesmerizing. It’s not just a cool piece of decor; it’s a fully playable instrument that brings a piece of my favorite game into the real world. This print perfectly encapsulated the blend of technology, art, and nostalgia that makes 3D printing so exciting.

I’m only just getting started on this journey, and I’m already brainstorming my next projects. Whether it’s practical tools for my workshop or fun creations inspired by my hobbies, I can’t wait to see what this machine can do. Stay tuned for more updates!

item.content:encoded:
Are you ready to revolutionize your approach to coding without getting bogged down in endless complexities? Whether you’re a budding developer, a seasoned freelancer, or anyone who works with code, understanding Git and GitHub is no longer optional – it’s essential. That’s why I’m thrilled to announce the release of my new book, “The GitHub Handbook”!

Why Git and GitHub, Simplified?

In today’s fast-paced world of software development, collaboration and efficient project management are key. But let’s be honest, diving into version control can feel overwhelming. That’s where “The GitHub Handbook” comes in. This isn’t a bloated tome; it’s a concise and practical guide designed to cut through the noise and get you straight to the core concepts.

Git, the industry-standard version control system, allows you to track every change to your code, revert to previous versions, and experiment without fear. GitHub, the leading platform for code collaboration, takes these capabilities to the next level, providing powerful tools for team-based development, code reviews, and project organization. My handbook simplifies learning these indispensable tools, giving you the confidence to master the basics and beyond.

What Awaits You Inside “The GitHub Handbook”?

This book is designed to be your comprehensive yet digestible guide, taking you from the absolute fundamentals to advanced techniques, all while keeping clarity and conciseness at the forefront. Here’s a glimpse of what you’ll master:

  • Core Concepts Made Easy: Demystify version control and understand why it’s the backbone of any successful project, presented in an easy-to-grasp manner.
  • The Streamlined Git Workflow: Learn the essential cycle of making, staging, and committing changes, building a clean and readable project history without unnecessary jargon.
  • Seamless Collaboration, Explained Simply: Dive into the art of teamwork with branching, merging, conflict resolution, and the power of GitHub’s pull request system for effective code review – all broken down into clear steps.
  • Beyond Code – Project Management at a Glance: Discover how to leverage GitHub’s features like Issues, Projects, and Wikis to manage tasks, track bugs, and keep your documentation organized and accessible, quickly and efficiently.
  • Advanced Techniques, Unpacked: Elevate your Git skills with powerful commands like git rebase for a cleaner history and git stash for temporarily saving unfinished work, presented with practical examples.
  • Automation with GitHub Actions – The Basics: Get a foundational understanding of how to automate repetitive tasks like testing and deploying your code, saving you time and effort with a straightforward introduction.

Who Will Benefit from This Concise Handbook?

“The GitHub Handbook” is crafted for a diverse audience, specifically those seeking a straightforward path to mastery:

  • Students: Lay a rock-solid foundation for your coding career, whether you’re in computer science or self-learning, with a book that respects your time.
  • Beginner Developers: Quickly get up to speed with the professional tools used by developers worldwide, without getting overwhelmed.
  • Freelancers and Solo Project Builders: Maintain a pristine project history, ensure your work is backed up, and effortlessly manage different project versions – a perfect companion for independent creators.
  • Anyone Who Works with Code: From data scientists and designers to technical writers and researchers, if you need to track changes and manage your digital assets efficiently, this book is for you.

Ready for a Straightforward Path to Git and GitHub Mastery?

Don’t let version control intimidate you any longer. “The GitHub Handbook” provides a structured, clear, and concise path to mastering these essential tools.

Order your copy today on Amazon and embark on your journey to becoming a Git and GitHub master with ease!

Buy on Amazon

I can’t wait to hear how “The GitHub Handbook” helps you achieve your coding goals!

item.content:encoded:
Well, hello there! If you’re reading this, you’ve officially stumbled upon the very first post of my brand-new personal website. And to that, I say: welcome!

This has been a long time coming, and I’m incredibly excited to finally have a dedicated space to share my journey, thoughts, and creations with the world. Think of this as my little corner of the internet, a digital home base where you can get to know me a bit better.

So, what can you expect to find around here? Let’s take a quick tour:

About Me

Head over to the “About Me” section, and you’ll find a more in-depth look into who I am, what drives me, and perhaps a few fun facts you might not know. I believe in connecting with people on a personal level, and I hope this section helps you feel a little more acquainted.

My Projects

This is where things get really exciting! My “Projects” section will be a constantly evolving gallery of my work. From web development to hardware design, I’ll be showcasing the things I’m passionate about and the challenges I’ve enjoyed tackling. I’m a firm believer in learning by doing, and these projects are a testament to that philosophy. Get ready to dive in and see what I’ve been up to!

Contact Me

Got a question? A collaboration idea? Or just want to say hello? Don’t hesitate to reach out! The “Contact Me” form is the easiest way to get in touch. I’m always open to new connections and interesting conversations, so drop me a line anytime.

This website is more than just a collection of pages; it’s a living, breathing reflection of my growth and aspirations. I’ll be regularly updating the blog with new insights, sharing progress on my projects, and perhaps even delving into some behind-the-scenes glimpses of my creative process.

Thank you for being here at the very beginning of this new adventure. I’m thrilled to have you along for the ride, and I can’t wait to see where this journey takes us.

Stay tuned for more!

item.content:encoded:
I’m excited to announce the launch of the new University of Georgia Motorcycle Club website! As a proud alumnus and former member, I had a blast building this site to give back to a community that means a lot to me. Built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, the site is a central hub for all things related to the club, making it easier than ever for riders to connect and get involved.

A Hub for All Riders

The new site is designed to be as bold and adventurous as the club itself. You can find everything you need to know, from the club’s mission of promoting safe riding to a gallery of our best adventures on the road.

I’ve made it super simple to join the community. Whether you’re a student, an alum, or just a motorcycle enthusiast, you can easily find links to the club’s Instagram and GroupMe to stay updated on all rides and events.

A Little Surprise

As a fun little tribute to the club, I’ve hidden a small easter egg on the website. I’d love for you to explore the site and see if you can find it.

Hint

The easter egg is hidden in plain sight, somewhere in the footer. Try interacting with a certain part of the text down there—you might be surprised by what you find.

I hope this new site helps grow the UGA Motorcycle Club. It was a blast working on it, and I can’t wait to see what adventures the club gets up to next.

Join the Community

item.content:encoded:
Summary

md-preview is a command-line tool written in Rust that renders Markdown files directly in your terminal, applying syntax highlighting and formatting. It leverages pulldown-cmark for robust Markdown parsing and termcolor for rich, colored output.

Tired of leaving your terminal to view a simple Markdown file? Meet md-preview, a powerful new command-line tool written in Rust that brings beautiful, formatted Markdown directly to your terminal screen. It’s designed to be fast, efficient, and highly readable, so you can focus on your work without context switching.

Why md-preview?

While many tools exist for viewing Markdown, md-preview is built specifically for the terminal environment. It uses pulldown-cmark for fast and accurate Markdown parsing and termcolor to apply rich syntax highlighting and formatting. This isn’t just a simple text dump; md-preview understands the structure of your document, rendering elements like headings, bold text, lists, and even tables with distinct colors and proper alignment.

Key Features:

  • Customizable: You can choose to show or hide the original Markdown symbols (like # or **) and even center the content in your terminal for better readability.
  • Syntax Highlighting: Easily distinguish between different Markdown elements at a glance.
  • Table Rendering: Tables are rendered with clean borders and proper alignment, making them easy to read.

Usage

Once installed, you can use it right away:

  • To render a file with default settings:
md-preview README.md
  • To show the original Markdown symbols:
md-preview MyDocument.md --symbol
  • To center the content for a more focused view:
md-preview Notes.md --center 10

md-preview is perfect for anyone who works with Markdown files and wants a seamless, terminal-native viewing experience. It’s a testament to the power and performance of Rust.

I’d love for you to give it a try. Head over to the GitHub repository to get the code and start using md-preview today. Let me know what you think!

While it works on any system with PyAudio, its real value shines when used with hardware like the Raspberry Pi 4’s onboard digital-to-analog converter […]

The post Signal Generator appeared first on SC Makes.
item.content:encoded:
Summary

This Python script generates and plays a waveform (sine or square) of a specified frequency, duration, and amplitude using the pyaudio and numpy libraries.

I’m excited to share a new Python tool I’ve developed, SignalGenerator. This script is specifically designed with embedded systems in mind, providing a simple yet powerful way to generate and test audio waveforms. While it works on any system with PyAudio, its real value shines when used with hardware like the Raspberry Pi 4’s onboard digital-to-analog converter (DAC) for quick and easy signal testing.

Why SignalGenerator for Embedded Systems?

When working with embedded systems, you often need to generate test signals to verify hardware functionality, troubleshoot audio circuits, or calibrate sensors. Manually setting up a signal generator can be cumbersome. SignalGenerator simplifies this process by allowing you to create and output precise sine, square, or frequency sweep signals directly from the command line, turning your Raspberry Pi into a versatile signal source. This is particularly useful for engineers and hobbyists prototyping audio applications or testing the performance of their DAC and related circuitry.

Features and Usage

SignalGenerator is built on Python and uses NumPy for waveform generation and PyAudio for output. It’s lightweight and easy to install.

To get started, simply install the required libraries:

pip install numpy pyaudio argparse

The script’s command-line interface makes it easy to specify the exact signal you need.

Key Features:

  • Waveform Types: Generate sine waves, square waves, or a frequency sweep.
  • Customizable Parameters: Easily set the duration, frequency, and amplitude of your signal.
  • Frequency Sweep Mode: Test a range of frequencies to analyze the frequency response of your hardware. This mode is a game-changer for evaluating the performance of filters, amplifiers, or the DAC itself across different frequencies.

Example Usage on a Raspberry Pi:

  • Test your DAC with a 440 Hz sine wave: 
python siggen.py sine -f 440
  • Check a high-frequency filter’s performance with a 10-second sweep: 
python siggen.py sweep -f 1000 -e 20000 -s 500
  • Send a 1 kHz square wave to a connected circuit: 
python siggen.py square -f 1000

A Note on the Raspberry Pi DAC

The Raspberry Pi 4 has a built-in DAC that provides audio output through its 3.5mm jack. This DAC can be used as the output “sink” for SignalGenerator. By connecting a simple audio breakout cable to the Pi’s audio jack, you can easily probe the generated signal with an oscilloscope or feed it into another circuit. This direct, no-hassle approach makes SignalGenerator an invaluable tool for on-the-fly testing and development.

I encourage you to try out SignalGenerator on your next embedded systems project. You can find the full details and source code on the GitHub repository. I hope this tool helps streamline your workflow and makes testing your hardware a breeze!
